text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 fired for customer 'Acme Industrial' (private VPC). Alert: private-controlplane-heartbeat-gap > 3m, ~60% of onprem agents reporting 'no heartbeat'. Dedup key pd-ACME-9274. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/private-vpc-controlplane#heartbeat-gap

oncall-alex: ACK. picking this up — investigating agent connectivity to control plane. @sre-maria @eng-ops-jon assigning triage. I'll pull the control plane ingress metrics and recent deploys.

sre-maria: grabbing control-plane logs now. Quick note: I see a spike of TLS handshake failures coming from 10.11.0.0/16 (customer agent pool). Errors look like `tls: handshake timeout` and `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` on some nodes. No recent control plane deploys in the last 2h.

eng-ops-jon: running `journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200` on a couple of agent hosts via the customer jumpbox, here's the tail from host acme-agent-03:

```
Mar 28 09:12:04 redwood-agent[2123]: dial tcp 172.16.8.45:443: connect: connection reset by peer
Mar 28 09:12:04 redwood-agent[2123]: tls: handshake timeout
Mar 28 09:12:05 redwood-agent[2123]: agent heartbeat failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed
Mar 28 09:12:07 redwood-agent[2123]: cert reload failed: file not found: /etc/redwood/agent/certs/current.pem
```

eng-ops-jon: traceroute from agent to controlplane endpoint 34.201.45.12 shows RSTs around the customer firewall IP (10.11.0.1). Also seeing iptables DROP rules on host: `-A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP` (weird). Sharing full logs to private S3.

oncall-alex: thanks. @eng-platform-raj can you check the control-plane side TLS terminators? Also please confirm if the customer performed any firewall changes or cert rotations. @customer-success-liz can you ping the customer contact?

customer-success-liz: pinged Acme infra (infra-oncall@acme.com). They confirm they ran a firewall policy update at ~09:10 that accidentally added a restrictive egress rule for jumpbox range. They're undoing it now and asked for ETA. They report batch inference jobs failing since 09:11 UTC. They want a quick mitigation.

eng-platform-raj: looking at controlplane LB logs — we did see a backlog of SYNs from the acme subnet and then many connections reset. No cert rotation on our side. I can open a temporary alternative egress path (hosted-relay) to accept agent connections from that subnet if we flip the routing flag on the tenant. That will route agent control traffic via our hosted relay (falls back to our managed TLS termination). Need approval for tenant-level routing flip (read-only controlplane fallback).

oncall-alex: :+1: approve the routing flip for canary subset (2/8 agents) to verify. Do the flip and monitor for 5 minutes, then escalate to 50% if green.

eng-platform-raj: doing canary now. Command:

```
# canary flip for Acme tenant
redwood-cli tenant update --id acme-tenant --controlplane-fallback hosted-relay --canary 2
```

eng-platform-raj: canary report: agents acme-agent-02 and acme-agent-03 reconnected within 45s, heartbeats restored. Error rate from that subnet on controlplane drops from 86% -> 12% for those nodes. Monitoring cluster-level metrics.

eng-ops-jon: restarting agent service on nodes that still show stale certs to force reload of cert files. Command used:

```
ssh acme-jump "sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 50 --no-pager"
```

eng-ops-jon: result: restarts succeed on 5/8 nodes; 3/8 still show `cert reload failed: file not found`. Those nodes are on a different automation partition (old config) — pushing fix now.

sre-maria: checking heartbeat graph — overall heartbeat gap decreased to <5m across the tenant and the reconnect rate is good for nodes on fallback. Control plane latency for management RPCs improved from 750ms -> 120ms for canary group.

customer-success-liz: Acme infra confirms their firewall change has been rolled back. They see request success on their side for the jobs that retried. They reported partial recovery at 09:30 UTC after your canary flip. They still want confirmation that nothing else will be needed.

oncall-alex: planning: 1) complete tenant routing flip to hosted-relay (50%) to get broader reconnections, 2) push agent cert sync automation to remaining 3 nodes, 3) monitor for 15m, 4) roll back to private controlplane only after we confirm stability. Posting change window doc link: https://internal.redwood/changes/acme-tenant-2765

eng-platform-raj: performing 50% route shift now. Shifting traffic groups A/B as discussed.

incident-bot: escalation check: oncall ack age 00:08:15, policy requires level-2 notify at 00:10:00. Sending escalation to pagerduty-bot.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation routed to SRE level-2 oncall (sre-maria) — notification sent.

sre-maria: got it. Taking lead for SLA/customer updates. Will collect logs and open a ticket for RCA. Quick findings: root cause appears to be combination of (a) customer firewall policy change causing blocked egress to control-plane, (b) some agent hosts had stale cert paths due to an automation drift which prevented reload when connections restored. We'll need to coordinate a postmortem with Acme and update agent automation to guard against missing certs.

eng-ops-jon: automation fix applied to remaining nodes; I validated certs exist at `/etc/redwood/agent/certs/current.pem` and restarted the service. All 8/8 agents now show green heartbeats. Sample validation command and output:

```
# validation
for h in acme-agent-{01..08}; do ssh $h "curl -sS https://controlplane-host/_health | jq .status" || echo $h failed; done
# output
"ok"
"ok"
"ok"
... (8 total)
```

sre-maria: confirming: controlplane heartbeat latency stable, no sustained error budget burn. I'm marking this as mitigated in Slack but leaving PD incident open until postmortem.

customer-success-liz: Acme says bulk workloads resumed and latency back to baseline. They requested an incident summary and a 30-day follow-up review. Assigning CS owner: @customer-success-liz and SRE owner: @sre-maria.

oncall-alex: thanks team. Quick action items: - eng-platform to add a safety check to routing flip runbook - eng-ops to add cert existence check in agent deploy pipeline - SRE to produce RCA and timeline. I'll file the internal incident ticket: INC-2026-ACME-2765 and attach logs.

sre-maria: I'll start the RCA doc and schedule a 1h postmortem meeting. Preliminary timeline: 09:10 firewall change -> 09:12 agents fail -> 09:16 PD fired -> 09:20 canary flip started -> 09:30 partial recovery -> 09:36 full reconnections after cert sync -> 09:40 mitigated.

oncall-alex: closing thread here. Keeping PD incident open until RCA produced. If anything regresses please reopen. :white_check_mark:

customer-success-liz: note: Acme also asked for confirmation of audit logs for the firewall change — I've requested those from them, will attach to the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: pd-ACME-9274, mitigated-by: hosted-relay canary + cert sync, mitigation-timestamp: 2765550780. Postmortem owner: sre-maria.
